# Matchstick Primitives

> Headless, keyboard-first React parts for trading screens, with a plain-TypeScript core. Developer preview 0.0.11. Every example uses synthetic data.

- [README.md](README.md): the parts, a first chart, the core, your own data.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what an agent may do with this package, what to ask first, what not to do.
- [dist/index.d.ts](dist/index.d.ts): every part, prop and type, with doc comments.
- [dist/core/index.d.ts](dist/core/index.d.ts): the React-free core (geometry, studies, drawing model, CSV reader, key maps).
- [src/tokens.css](src/tokens.css): design tokens (`--mt-*`), imported as `@matchstick-trading/primitives/tokens.css`.
- Docs: https://ui.matchstick.trading/docs/getting-started
- Licence: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE). Source is in src/. Free building blocks for trading screens; issues are open at https://github.com/matchstick-trading/primitives/issues.
- Live demo: https://ui.matchstick.trading/docs/live (made-up data).
- Full screen: `Fullscreen.Frame` wraps the chart and `Fullscreen.Toggle` (inside it) enters and leaves; the browser's full screen where there is one, a full-page fallback otherwise (README, "Full screen"). Escape clears the chart's crosshair or selection first, then leaves.
- Selection: `Selection.Root`, `Selection.Layer`, `Series.Root`, `Series.Select`, `Series.Options` and an `id` on `Study.Line` / `Study.Band` give one selection (drawing, series or study). Rules and parts are in README.md, "Select the series and studies". Series options are the host's to fill.
- Series: a series is `{ id, label, points[] }` with `{ t, kind, v? }` points (ISO-8601 UTC `t`; kinds `value`, `missing`, `market-closed`, `not-applicable`, `halted`, `unknown`); `Panels.Root` and `Study.Line` take `points`; bare `values` is a shim that is still accepted in this version and will be removed in a later one. `csvAdapter`, `validateSeriesSet`, `report` are in the core. See README.md, "Give a series a clock".
- Panels: `Panels.Root` (series and bands), `Panels.Layer` (inside `Chart.Plot`), `Panels.List` and `Panels.Move` put more than one series on a chart in bands with their own price scales, and move a series between bands by buttons, not a drag. The bars, volume and drawings stay in the first band. Rules and parts are in README.md, "Panels and several series".
